claims.explanation: Gefitinib selectively kills cancer lines whose growth depends on EGFR signaling, most clearly those carrying activating EGFR kinase-domain mutations (exon 19 deletions or L858R) that make the receptor hypersensitive to inhibition, as seen in HCC4006, NCIH1650, and KYSE270. Lines without EGFR addiction, or with bypass resistance such as MET amplification or downstream MAPK/PI3K activation, are relatively spared. Expression of EGFR and its ligand/co-receptor network may further modulate sensitivity.

features.basis: Activating EGFR kinase-domain mutations predict gefitinib response (literature and observed in HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270)
EGFR dependency/expression required for EGFR-TKI sensitivity
MET amplification causes gefitinib resistance via ERBB3/PI3K; HGC27 (MET-mutant, least affected) supports this
KRAS mutations drive EGFR-independent MAPK signaling and are associated with poor EGFR-TKI response
BRAF mutations activate downstream MAPK and bypass EGFR dependence; many BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines are least affected
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT downstream of EGFR, reducing dependence on EGFR; PTEN-mutant lines appear among least affected
PIK3CA mutations can activate PI3K independently of EGFR, blunting EGFR-TKI sensitivity
NRAS mutations activate MAPK independently of EGFR; NRAS-mutant melanoma lines are least affected
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/MAPK downstream of EGFR, reducing EGFR dependence
ERBB3/HER3-dependent PI3K signaling is required for EGFR-mutant cell survival and can mediate sensitivity
MEK1 mutations activate MAPK downstream of EGFR; NCIH1437 (MAP2K1-mutant) appears in both lists but is not strongly killed
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines and may reflect general genomic instability rather than EGFR dependence
